text: End of course test, track two. Today you are going to present your research into scientists who have had an impact on astronomy and how we understand the stars and planets. So we'll begin with Yoko who is going to talk about Isaac Newton, then Walid is going to tell us about Carl Sagan. Sir Isaac Newton was an English scientist who lived from 1643 to 1727. He is one of the most remarkable scientists who ever lived. Of course he lived a long time before humans started exploring space, but he helped us to start to understand it better. He invented a new kind of telescope, an object for looking at the stars, which meant people could see them more clearly. Some of Newton's work is not very easy to understand unless you are a mathematician. His book, The Principles of Mathematics, explained the movement of the planets around the sun. It was an amazing achievement which changed people's ideas about physics. At the time we believed that the sun moved around the earth. Because Newton's ideas were so new and different, they made some people very angry. So it's perhaps not surprising that later in life Newton stopped showing people his work. Although everyone remembers Newton as a great scientist, he had some strange ideas too. Like many people at the time, Newton tried to change ordinary metal into gold and did lots of research about it. Carl Sagan was an American astronomer who lived from 1934 to 1996. His scientific achievements are not quite as amazing as Newton's or Einstein's. However, Sagan knew how to explain complicated scientific ideas so that people could understand them. He wrote popular books about astronomy and had a TV show called The Cosmos in the 1980s. Because he was very excited about astronomy, he was able to show ordinary people how exciting it is too. A talent that not many scientists have. The show had 135 million viewers from all over the world, which even today is quite a few people. However, some astronomers believed that Carl Sagan couldn't be so popular and a serious scientist at the same time. This was made worse when Sagan became one of the first scientists to talk about global warming. At the time, no one understood his ideas very well. And it became another reason why other scientists disliked him.
